questions.text: Acceptance criteria 3, 4 and 5 of REQ-339 require positions and preferences to persist across sign-out, sign-in and later visits. WI-030 explicitly leaves out positions and preferences storage (no such tables exist in the repo). Should TC-015 (a) leave these criteria out and have a follow-up test case cover them once storage exists, or (b) verify them now against a stand-in resource? If (b), which resource should be used?
questions.reason: No storage exists for positions or preferences, so the expected outcomes for those criteria cannot be written without guessing.

questions.text: REQ-339 says the client stores the JWT and sends it in the Authorization header. WI-030 uses an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie instead. Should the test cases verify the cookie transport (the WI-030 plan), or the Authorization header (the requirement wording)?
questions.reason: The two transports produce different expected outcomes for sign-in, session persistence and sign-out. The WI-030 risks say the product owner should confirm this change.

questions.text: What counts as a strong password for sign-up? Please give the minimum length and any required character classes, and say whether a breached-password check applies.
questions.reason: REQ-339 and WI-030 say strong password without defining it, so the weak-password and boundary scenarios cannot be written.

questions.text: Ownership scenarios need a resource that belongs to a user. WI-030 says the Note table has no owner column and may get a user_id in the migration, or be flagged as not user-scoped. Which applies, and which resource should the cross-user access test use?
questions.reason: The ownership test (a user cannot read another user's resource) needs a concrete resource and its owner field.
